intro: The commodities I keep an eye on, from crude oil and LNG to metals and freight, plus the macro drivers behind them. Prices refresh automatically every hour on weekdays, with a short note each morning on what moved oil and gas and why.
note: Data: Yahoo Finance and FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis). Energy and metals prices are front-month futures. For information only, not investment advice
my_take:
The oil market is still tight, and the futures curve tells us that quite clearly. Brent's front month is trading about US$12.50 a barrel above the contract six months out, which means buyers are paying a big premium to get oil now rather than later. As long as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains disrupted, I do not see that premium going away quickly.

At the same time, diesel is where the real squeeze is. US distillate stocks are about 6% below their five-year average, even with refineries running at close to full capacity. Hence, refining margins are still fairly wide, although they have come off over the past month. In gas, Asia and Europe are paying almost the same price for LNG, so cargoes have little reason to favour one region over the other for now.

What should we watch? Sunday's OPEC+ meeting, any news on shipping through Hormuz, and whether US diesel stocks finally start to rebuild.
